scope: R199: the video VAE wastes 58 percent of its decode work on overlapping temporal chunks

code_structure.pattern: decode_temporal loops over num_chunks serially; each chunk takes tokens_chunk_size + token_overlap latent frames through _adaptive_decode, and adjacent chunks overlap by token_overlap before blending

geometry.finding: 58 percent of decode work goes into overlapping frames that are then discarded by blend

best.note: also cuts chunk count from 7 to 2, removing five chunk-level fixed costs

candidates_ranked.recommendation: safest first step and already clears the target

two_blocking_caveats.detail: changing tokens_chunk_size changes which frames take part in the overlap blend and changes the temporal convolution context length, so outputs differ; per contract it must be disabled, reported and decided by the user

activation memory grows with chunk length: chunk_size=5 peaks at 13.436 GiB while chunk_size=18 decodes 80 frames per chunk (2.9x); a rough total of about 19 GiB may still fit on a 32 GiB card but this is unmeasured

significance: the video VAE target may need only one temporal-chunk parameter change, with no kernel work at all
limits: pure arithmetic with no machine run or measurement; the payoff depends on per-chunk cost scaling linearly
the num_chunks formula was reverse-engineered from the loop and not checked against the code that computes it
whether isolated head/tail frames affect num_chunks was not verified
memory sufficiency was not tested and is the largest uncertainty
the change is numerically non-equivalent and needs a user decision
